correctness.rationale: The exact star-preservation probability is a convex combination of j/(j+1) for one step and 1/(j+1) for zero steps. It yields the survival product and all endpoints. A nonstar remains a nonstar as edges only accumulate. Gamma ratios, summable geometric bounds, exact tail sums, and small-parameter logarithmic expansions prove the mean transition and both weak limits. The packaged exact checker separately enumerated graph transitions for small cases and passed 4694 assertions; finite checks are not substituted for proof.

The closest alternative is the generic product formula for inhomogeneous hazards, which does not supply the model-specific star hazard or asymptotic regimes. Earlier implicit coverage remains possible.

value.rationale: The source paper explicitly relies on eventual escape from initial stars to study global leaf growth. Quantifying that natural escape reveals that it has infinite expected duration at pure one-step attachment and finite but logarithmically divergent expected duration under arbitrarily small zero-step contamination. The sharp q~1/s interpolation between Lomax and exponential lifetimes is a structural finite-size/noise boundary with implications for interpreting finite-time experiments and exceptional seed removal. This is motivated by the model, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
